title: Route one undeliverable subscription to a dead-letter queue
prompt: An SNS topic has an email subscription and two SQS subscriptions. Because of a permissions change, notifications that SNS cannot deliver to one of the SQS queues are currently lost. Without changing the email subscription or the other SQS subscription, you want to retain messages that still cannot be delivered to the affected subscription after retries in a queue for investigation. Where should you configure this?

choices.text: Have the publisher inspect the success response from Publish and use it to determine whether each individual subscription received the message.
choices.explanation: A successful Publish response means SNS accepted the message; it does not confirm delivery to each subscription.

choices.text: Set the RedrivePolicy on the failing SNS subscription to point to an investigation SQS queue, and allow SNS to send messages to it.
choices.explanation: This routes failed deliveries to a dead-letter queue for that subscription, while the healthy subscriptions can continue without configuration changes.

choices.text: Enable only SNS delivery status logging and reconstruct the message body from the log entries.
choices.explanation: Delivery status logs help investigate results, but they do not retain the original undelivered message in a queue.

choices.text: Set only a RedrivePolicy on the destination SQS queue based on its receive-failure count.
choices.explanation: A message that never reached the SQS queue has no SQS receive count.

source.label: SNSのデッドレターキュー

learning.reason: SNS delivery failures are different from processing failures after a message has arrived in SQS.
learning.concept: A subscription's RedrivePolicy can retain messages that SNS failed to deliver to that subscription.
